thread: The ward-stones read wrong: hitched hum and cold inside

evidence.clue: The noon stone on the southern track hums with a late, hitching beat and cold under its warmth; Sylvanas felt it by bare palm. Lor'themar felt nothing.
The magisters' wardens' spring report called the ring stable 'in three different hands'.
Jaina told the watch the stones are sick from the inside and wardens read only the outsides.

Jaina to Sylvanas: the same residue and drag in the pulse is in the ward-stones, tied in through the currents; the worst stones are on the second ring either side of the high road, plus one on the outer ring at the creek bend.
The cell stone hums with a late, dragging tail; a wedge stone below it presses on her magic; the rings muffle the contamination for anyone inside; outside the line it hits full.
The wards did not stop the contamination: the stones have been feeding it into the Pass.

Chapter 3: Sylvanas still carries the noon stone's 'cold under its warmth' in her palm ('since yesterday'); she knows 'her line was north, and the stones were north'. The dead's cow way points at the stretch of outer ring between the Pass and the eastern posts, where a warden goes round once a fortnight with a lens; her dispatch asks for the wardens on that stretch to be doubled and eyes put on the high ground.

Elves cannot feel the contamination: Sylvanas lays her hand on her mare's neck and finds 'Nothing in the hide or the bones of her hand. There never was.' Horses at the ring stones sidestep once and stand (Ch1-2); in Millhaven the mare backs and pins her ears, a stronger sign than any ward-stone.

Chapter 6 (horse ladder, next rung): on the walled Andorhal approach Sylvanas's horse stops dead, throws up its head and goes sideways into the wall, scraping her boot; Cyndia's half turns, ears flat; Jaina's mare backs and sidesteps toward the ditch. 'At the ring stones on the border the horses had done this once and then stood, ears forward. These went on shying.' Sylvanas talks to hers low and steady in Thalassian; Cyndia speaks into her horse's ear; both move on crabwise, tossing heads, whites of eyes showing. Elves feel nothing themselves.

readerKnows: The ward ring is in the dead's line of march; wardens remain the magisters' lens-and-ledger type; the stones are tied to the contamination.
povCharacterKnows: Sylvanas: the noon stone is wrong; the dead march at the ring; she cannot feel the contamination in anything but a stone.
notes: Do not suddenly make the elves feel it. The ring's effect (muffling versus conducting) remains open. Chapter 9 (project outline) burns Millhaven's dead on the border runestones; Ch3's cow way heading toward the ring supports that.
